name: plate_steel
summary: Armour plate: hammered, curved, and worn where it is hit. Not a blade.
why: Split off from steel after the Plate gauntlets were looked at in the engine wearing
it. A blade's grain is brushed and directional because a blade is ground along its
length, and on a gauntlet that direction means nothing: the UV islands of a hand run
every way at once, so a grain that is long in V smeared across the fingers in one
direction and across the cuff in another. It read as motion blur.
Plate is hammered instead. The surface is isotropic — dents and planishing marks with
no direction to them — which is what `cast` already generates, and it survives being
laid out across a hand because it looks the same whichever way the island faces.
armour is not, and a piece that has been worn is duller still. The gap between this
and the blade's 0.32 is most of what makes a sword read as sharper than the hand
holding it, which is the correct relationship.

Roughness 0.68, swept in the engine on ArmorMale10 under the grazing sun and raised from 0.42. See MU2/tests/materials.sh. Across 0.13 to 0.85 the low end is oily - the cast pitting reads as a wet sheen rather than as a surface - and 0.42 sat near enough to it that the chest's bands and the skirt's panels barely showed. At 0.68 the form reads and the edges still catch a bright highlight, which is what keeps it metal. Past 0.8 it goes chalky through the middle of the chest.

That it wanted raising rather than lowered is the material's own summary being taken seriously: this is armour that has been hit, not a blade that has been ground. A mirror finish on battle plate is the mistake the separate blade steel exists to avoid.

Roughness 0.52 and depth 0.05, moved together, and the pair is the point. The 0.68 sweep ran while the engine had no environment specular at all - Interior on the probe and the sky off as a reflection source - so 'the low end is oily' was a judgement of a metal with nothing to reflect. With reflections fixed the plate at 0.68 reads flat, and dropping roughness alone turns the cast pitting into per-texel glitter: at depth 0.12 every pit is its own sun glint. Same failure the Kris hit, same medicine - the grain shallower as the surface gets glossier, so the pitting stays a disturbance in the highlight rather than a field of sparks.

f0 0.50 with f0_from_art 0.5, and this is the balance pass, judged in Blender on a three-way lineup - stock, this, and a 0.35-roughness chrome-leaning trial - beside a chrome ball over a checkered ground. Without the correction the plate hands the renderer MU's painting raw (0.335 mean linear where steel is ~0.56) and reads as plaster whatever the roughness. At the axe's 0.35 art weight the set turns silver and the emblem washes out; at 0.5 the reflectance is steel's and the sheet's bands, straps and chest relief stay legible, which for armour is the identity of the set. f0 a step under the blade's 0.56 because plate is worn, not ground.

roughness_range 0.12 -> 0.06. The last of the yellow specks on the pauldron were not the probe (a calm probe-only ground changed 154k pixels and left them) and not the sheets (unshaded is clean) - they are the deepest grain pits reaching roughness 0.40, where a grazing Fresnel hands them a concentrated sample of the dome's warm ground colour and the grade saturates it yellow. Halving the range keeps the pitting's variation in the highlight and takes the deep-gloss tail off it.

f0 0.575, roughness 0.34, f0_desaturation 0.75 - the 'looks like plate steel' pass, found on the assembled five-piece set in Blender under the recreated bench rig (same dome, sun, ambient, turf) and migrated here. The first try was a plain brightness gain and came out porcelain: steel is not bright, it is contrasty, and what sells it is the dome's gradient sweeping a curved plate. So the value gain eased to 1.15 (f0 0.50 -> 0.575), the art pulled a quarter toward grey (a painted sheet's warmth reflects as a permanent tint - steel that reflects orange reads as dirty brass), and the roughness dropped to 0.34 so the reflection has edges. That is knowingly near the blade's 0.32: the set's owner asked for shining plate, and the note above about worn armour yields to that ask - marked as the taste decision it is.
